title: Antifungal Activity of Natural Compounds and Therapeutic Potential of Allicin–Cinnamaldehyde Combination Against Pet Malassezia Pachydermatis
content: Malassezia is a common fungus and one of the zoonotic pathogens. It is a common disease among pets including cats, which usually parasitizes the skin surfaces under suitable environmental conditions. Management of Malassezia dermatitis relies mainly on antifungal drugs. Repeated or prolonged usage may be accompanied by reduced susceptibility and concerns about recurrence. Natural compounds may offer advantages in the management of superficial fungal skin disease. In this study, thirty-eight clinical samples were collected from pet cats with Malassezia-associated skin lesions and a KM mouse dermatitis model was established for in vivo evaluation. Three M. pachydermatis isolates were screened against 11 antibiotics and 14 natural compounds. The most resistant Malassezia pachydermis strain SZ06 was selected for minimum inhibitory concentration determination using checkerboard assays, growth-curve analysis, scanning electron microscopy after treatment, and genome annotation. Plant-derived compound allicin, cinnamaldehyde, eugenol, and anisaldehyde showed significant antifungal activity. Checkerboard assays showed the strongest synergistic effect for allicin plus cinnamaldehyde, reducing the minimum inhibitory concentrations of allicin and cinnamaldehyde to one-eighth and one-quarter of their single-agent values, respectively. For the regression mice infected with SZ06, topical treatment with 0.5% allicin plus 0.5% cinnamaldehyde produced the best therapeutic response, improving lesions, fungal clearance, histopathology, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Genome sequencing of SZ06 suggested that this isolate carried multiple candidate genes involved in efflux, membrane transport, and drug-response pathways. The natural compound allicin-cinnamaldehyde combination demonstrated promising antifungal activity, representing a potential topical therapy for Malassezia dermatitis in pet cats.
